project: Mission Forge (Pinous) — NASA Space Apps 2026, Space Mission Design Game

requirements.requirement: A continuation mechanism that keeps this session working until 08:00 KST, honours a stop file, and is actually verified
requirements.verify: Pipe test of the hook for continue / other session / stop file; in-session probe that project hooks load
requirements.expected: Hook blocks a stop before the end time and lets it through with the stop file
requirements.actual: Hook pipe-tested (continue / other session / stop file); a temporary PostToolUse probe in the same settings file fired in this session, proving project hooks are loaded live. It covers the session ending a turn early, not a crashed process or a usage limit.

requirements.requirement: Requirements traceability table and state files kept current
requirements.verify: Files exist and are updated as work proceeds
requirements.expected: Every required item has a status and evidence
requirements.actual: requirements.json (53 items), WORK_STATE.json, WORK_LOG.jsonl, NIGHTSHIFT_BRIEF.md, docs/ADDED_DECISIONS.md, reports/evidence/ maintained through the run

requirements.requirement: One connected play flow: goal → requirements → design → trade-offs → build/connect/control → test → fly/operate → faults → science result
requirements.userPath: Lobby → mission → define → design → My AI → Fly → Submit
requirements.verify: Browser E2E through the whole flow
requirements.expected: A crew can go from a new mission to a scored debrief
requirements.actual: The whole flow from goal to evaluated result is connected in the real UI (full-flow run) and through the API for two other missions

requirements.requirement: Adding an instrument ripples into power, mass, data and cost, and on into comms, launch and schedule
requirements.userPath: Parts → Add → Connect; watch goals and limits
requirements.verify: Unit test + API test of derived results before/after
requirements.expected: Power load, mass, data, cost, launch margin and schedule all change
requirements.actual: Adding two instruments changed harness mass, total mass, load, power margin, depth of discharge, data generated, cost (over cap by $0.3M), schedule and launch margin in one preview

requirements.requirement: A mission starts built: goals, limits, environment, parts, ports, lines, initial state, the problem, adjustable values with units and ranges
requirements.userPath: Create mission in lobby; open it
requirements.verify: Unit test: every scenario is wired, validated and playable at start
requirements.expected: Wiring check passes at start; kit lists levers and parts
requirements.actual: generateMission prewires every starting part; kit with levers (units, ranges in the UI), toolbox and roles; wiring check passes at start for all scenarios

requirements.requirement: Mission package is validated after generation (schema, ids, units, connections, executability, goal logic)
requirements.expected: Invalid packages are refused; every scenario/difficulty is finishable
requirements.actual: Schema + referential + wiring + controller validation on every generated mission; every scenario and difficulty finishable in the playability test

requirements.requirement: Different missions really differ in world, limits and rules
requirements.verify: Unit test + API: three scenarios, different bodies, catalogues, objectives, events
requirements.expected: Different central body, parts, goals, results
requirements.actual: Three missions differ in body, bus, limits, duration, ground station, catalogue, goals, events and outcome (CubeSat vs Mars run)

requirements.requirement: Each player has their own AI conversation context
requirements.userPath: My AI panel: ask, then follow up with 'do it'
requirements.verify: Unit test with a scripted model + live model dialogue
requirements.expected: Follow-ups resolve against that player's own earlier turns only
requirements.actual: Scripted-model test: each player's prompt carries that player's earlier turns and none of the other's; live run: a 4th request extended the controller from the 3rd

requirements.requirement: A conversation with one's AI is private by default; shared-world changes are visible to all; the owner can share
requirements.verify: API + WebSocket test with two accounts
requirements.expected: Other crew see only a stub until shared
requirements.actual: Two real browsers: Ben's crew view shows 'Ana & their AI — a private conversation' with none of the text; after Ana clicks Share with crew he reads question and answer. HTTP/WebSocket redaction covered by tests.

requirements.requirement: The AI reads the live world (config, derived results, wiring, catalogue, goals) before answering
requirements.userPath: Ask 'why is data not coming down?'
requirements.expected: Answer cites current numbers
requirements.actual: Live answers quote current derived values (data rate, link margin, storage, catalogue prices)

requirements.requirement: Hypotheses: sound → built and measured; wrong → explained with reasons and alternatives; outside the model → limits stated
requirements.userPath: Ask 'if we had X could we Y?'
requirements.expected: No false success
requirements.actual: Sound ideas are built and measured (e05/e06 run); a wrong idea is refused with numbers and options; an out-of-model idea is answered with the model's limit; an impossible controller signal never reaches a proposal

requirements.requirement: 'Created' means real object ids, applied changes and measured results; change summary and undo are available
requirements.userPath: My AI reply shows what changed; Log → roll back
requirements.expected: Reply lists ids and before→after; rollback restores
requirements.actual: Replies list what was built with before→after numbers; proposals list created ids (components, lines, controllers); rollback to an earlier version is in the Log tab and tested

requirements.requirement: On a validation failure the AI analyses the reason and retries
requirements.verify: Unit test with a scripted model that first returns an invalid line
requirements.expected: Second attempt is accepted; third failure is reported honestly
requirements.actual: A rejected line goes back to the model with the validator's reason; the corrected attempt is accepted (repairs=1); three rejections end in an honest 'could not' with the reason and no change

requirements.requirement: Parts are executable components with id, type, ports, unit-typed properties, state, constraints, connections, history, provenance
requirements.expected: Ports and lines shown per part
requirements.actual: Part card in the real UI lists each port with its kind, unit, the line plugged in and what it carries of its rating; unconnected ports are flagged

requirements.requirement: Lines carry real flows (power W, data bit/s, control); incompatible ports are refused; undersized lines limit the part
requirements.userPath: Part card → Connect; AI adds a line
requirements.expected: Unwired part does nothing; bad line rejected with reason; clipped flow
requirements.actual: Unwired part draws and measures nothing; power-only draws but records nothing; incompatible lines refused with reasons; a 3x array behind its old line is clipped until the line is refitted

requirements.requirement: AI-generated control logic is new behaviour that actually runs and changes data/power results
requirements.userPath: Ask AI for a controller → approve → Fly
requirements.expected: Flight KPIs differ with the controller
requirements.actual: Unit tests and a live-model run both show flight KPIs change when a controller is installed

requirements.requirement: Safety: schema/type/unit checks, bounded evaluation, no file/network/secret access, test before apply, atomic apply, rollback; no eval
requirements.where: src/systems/expr.ts (own parser, bounded), src/pipeline/proposals.ts (flight test), src/state/store.ts
requirements.expected: Hostile input is rejected and the world is unchanged
requirements.actual: Hostile expressions rejected by the parser; a controller with an unknown signal never reaches a proposal; new control logic is flown before it is offered; publish is atomic through the versioned store

requirements.requirement: Results are computed by the authoritative engine, not by the language model
requirements.expected: LLM never sets a score
requirements.actual: Scores, checks, outcome and flight KPIs come from recalc/simulation/scoring; the model only words replies. Unit tests assert numbers independent of any model.

requirements.requirement: Reproducible: same design, seed and events give the same flight
requirements.expected: Identical KPIs
requirements.actual: Same design and events give identical KPIs on repeat runs

requirements.requirement: Shared simulation time: speed, pause, step, re-run are shared by the crew
requirements.expected: Both clients show the same moment
requirements.actual: Shared clock: play/pause, three speeds, step ±1 h/±1 d (stepped exactly one day in the browser), slider; one player's clock reaches the other three; the flight result is shared and reproducible

requirements.requirement: Save and compare designs before/after under the same conditions; failed hypotheses are kept with reasons
requirements.expected: Comparison table; refused ideas listed with reasons
requirements.actual: Two saved designs compared side by side (14 rows); an idea the AI turned down is kept under 'Did not hold' with its reason and can be shared with the crew; other players then read it

requirements.requirement: Mission success and its evidence are shown first; the score is secondary; game assumptions are labelled
requirements.userPath: Top of the left column; debrief
requirements.expected: Success conditions with evidence before points
requirements.actual: 'Does the mission work?' with four conditions and their evidence is above the points in the left column and in the debrief; the rule is stated as a game rule

requirements.requirement: Web and MR share one mission, objects, wiring and simulation
requirements.verify: IWER emulator E2E (not a physical headset)
requirements.expected: Changes cross both ways
requirements.actual: Same page, same mission state, same engine for desktop and immersive session; verified both ways in the WebXR emulator (13 checks) and the E2E suite. Level of verification: emulator.

requirements.requirement: Personal view (camera) is not shared; design state is
requirements.userPath: Rotate the view in one client
requirements.expected: Other client's camera does not move
requirements.actual: Camera state is never sent; only presence, design edits and the mission clock are shared (two-browser run)

requirements.requirement: Verified on a physical MR headset
requirements.actual: No physical headset can be operated from this session. Tracking, passthrough, hand input, frame rate and comfort on a real Quest are not verified. To verify: open https://<host>:8787/mission on the headset browser over HTTPS (TLS_CERT_FILE/TLS_KEY_FILE) and run the checklist in the report.

requirements.requirement: Up to four players: join, leave, reconnect with state restored
requirements.expected: Fifth is refused; reconnect restores
requirements.actual: Three join, the fifth is refused with 409; a client that dropped and came back is at the current version

requirements.requirement: Ordering, versions, duplicate protection, conflict handling, AI re-validation on a moved version
requirements.expected: Stale edits rejected; proposals rebased
requirements.actual: Same-value simultaneous edits: one applied, the other told who changed it; different-value edits both apply; invalid line refused for all; proposals are re-evaluated when the mission moved

requirements.requirement: Sync latency and state equality measured across four clients
requirements.expected: Latency numbers and identical state hashes recorded
requirements.actual: Loopback, n=72: edit sent → received by another client median 4.3 ms, p95 6.8 ms, max 7.5 ms (includes recalculation); state hashes identical

requirements.requirement: History of who changed what, and undo
requirements.expected: History lists author and summary; rollback works
requirements.actual: Version history with author and summary; rollback restricted to the lead and audited

requirements.requirement: A newcomer sees the mission, what is wrong, what can be changed, what to ask, what a change did, and the end condition
requirements.expected: All six are on screen without digging
requirements.actual: Reviewed the first-screen capture: problem and crux, 'Does the mission work?' with what is missing and the end condition, controls/parts/crew kit with reasons, My AI with example asks, a 7-step walkthrough, metric tiles with explanations on hover

requirements.requirement: No dead buttons, unexplained numbers, unexplained rotation or fake progress
requirements.expected: No console errors; states are real
requirements.actual: Scan of every tab as lead and as a second member (18 views, ~50 controls each): no unlabeled control, no disabled control without a stated reason, no page errors; the idle bus spin was removed and the spacecraft's display pace is labelled; progress shown is the pipeline's real task states

requirements.requirement: Accounts/API/device survey; .env.example and README match the code; no secrets in repo, bundle, logs or report
requirements.verify: grep for secrets; read config code
requirements.expected: Table in the report
requirements.actual: .env.example rewritten from the variables the code actually reads (public/secret marked); .env is git-ignored and untracked; no key string in tracked files, evidence or report (checked by grep and by the report builder)

requirements.requirement: Autonomous additions recorded with reason, alternatives, impact, verification
requirements.actual: 13 decisions recorded with reason, alternatives, impact and verification

requirements.requirement: Final report as .md and a rendered, checked .pdf with Korean text
requirements.expected: Readable PDF, no clipped tables
requirements.actual: Report built as .md and .pdf; PDF checked: page count, Korean text extracted, no broken images, no overflowing tables, no empty pages, no secret-looking strings; page pictures reviewed

requirements.requirement: A new mission arrives with environment, systems, limits and goals built
requirements.actual: A new mission arrives with world, limits, goals, parts, ports, lines (all connected), checks, a problem statement and a kit of controls, parts and roles

requirements.requirement: The real UI takes a crew from design through operation to evaluation
requirements.actual: One player, real UI clicks and typing, live model: define → add 2 parts → connect → AI control logic → refuted idea → launch vehicle → clock step → fly → compare designs → review → submit → debrief (16 checks, no console errors)

requirements.requirement: Selecting a part shows its real properties, connections, state and meaning
requirements.actual: Selecting the neutron spectrometer shows mass, cost, draw, data rate, on-time, three ports, their lines (12.0 W of 15.0 W; 2000 bit/s of 10.0k bit/s) and its state

requirements.requirement: The AI reads the current world and explains a cause
requirements.actual: Live model (gpt-6-astra) read the mission: 0 Gb/day returned because no instrument is on board; downlink 51.84 Gb/day, margin 30.6 dB; nothing was changed

requirements.requirement: Different phrasings create new parts, lines and control functions
requirements.actual: Live model built two instruments with their 6 lines, a part resize, and control logic from three differently worded Korean requests; real ids listed in each proposal

requirements.requirement: Generated control logic runs and the system result changes
requirements.actual: Live model's controller flown for 365 days on the same events: negative-power days 155 → 0, instruments forced off 127 → 0, data returned 11581.8 → 10950.5 Gb (the cost of saving power)

requirements.requirement: A wrong hypothesis gets reasons and alternatives, never a false success
requirements.actual: Live model: 'paint the array black to improve the link' → No, with the reason, the current margin (10.24 dB vs 3 dB), and three alternatives with their costs; nothing built, world unchanged

requirements.requirement: A hypothesis outside the model is answered with the model's limits
requirements.actual: Live model: wiper against Mars dust → the spacecraft is in a 400 km orbit, expected recovery 0 W, and 'the model has no dust-deposition loss'; nothing built

requirements.requirement: Adding equipment changes cost, mass, power, comms and mission result
requirements.actual: Same run: mass 125.21→148.32 kg, load 113.5→128.8 W, data 0→52.0 Gb/day (over the 51.84 Gb/day downlink), cost over cap, schedule 29.6 of 36 months

requirements.requirement: Four independent clients see the same state and result
requirements.actual: Four real WebSocket+HTTP clients: identical state hashes on sockets and over HTTP, same flight result, same final state

requirements.requirement: A Web change appears in MR and an MR change appears on the Web
requirements.actual: IWER emulator: a part added on the web appears in the headset scene and status; Connect and Fly pressed in the headset reach the web; control logic installed on the web is named in the headset; lines drawn are the same on both. Emulator only — not a physical headset.

requirements.requirement: Rotating one's own view does not disturb others or the mission
requirements.actual: Ana orbits her camera (moved 4.84 units); Ben's camera moved 0.000000 and the mission version stayed v1

requirements.requirement: Concurrent edits, duplicate requests, reconnect and server restart recover as designed
requirements.actual: Concurrent same-value edits (one wins, other told), different-value edits (both apply), reconnect (restored), server restart (accounts, sessions, versions, pending proposals restored and approvable)

requirements.requirement: Bad code, endless loops and forbidden access cannot damage the shared world
requirements.actual: process.exit, constructor escapes, loops, deep nesting, oversize input all rejected as ExprError; invalid controller blocked at validation; world version unchanged

requirements.requirement: AI/API errors, network loss and failed generation can be retried and recovered
requirements.actual: Model failure: request fails honestly, world unchanged, next request works (test). Network drop in the browser: the client reconnects and catches up to an edit made while it was offline.

requirements.requirement: Designs can be compared before/after under the same conditions and the result reproduced
requirements.actual: Same design flown twice gives identical KPIs; designs saved and compared side by side in the browser E2E (14 rows)

requirements.requirement: A mission with different conditions also generates, plays and evaluates
requirements.actual: CubeSat (Earth, 12.3 kg, $3.1M) and Mars orbiter (493 kg, $466M, 687 days) each generated, wired, flown with their own events, and submitted with an outcome and score; different catalogues, goals and results

requirements.requirement: The final build starts from a clean procedure and the core play is reproduced
requirements.actual: Web client rebuilt from an empty build folder; server started on a spare port with a new empty data folder; a lunar mission played to submission (9 checks) and the wiring loop in a real browser (9 checks) both passed

requirements.requirement: The final PDF is generated, opened and checked
requirements.actual: PDF generated with headless Edge, text extracted with pdftotext, pages rendered to pictures and inspected; service table and evidence paths present
